raw_response:
I will keep my farm centered on the wheat-maize rotation because that is the most stable part of my business, it matches my land and irrigation, and it is easier to manage with only part of the family available for farm work. I will keep most of the land in winter wheat followed by summer maize, then use a smaller share for higher-value crops that give me cash flow but do not take over the whole farm. I will put cotton on a moderate area because it is familiar and spreads risk, and I will keep chili and watermelon at sizes I can still manage with more labor and spraying. I will keep stevia and broccoli smaller because they can make money, but I do not want too much area in crops that need tighter management and marketing. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water to protect yield on the cash crops first and keep grain yields steady on the main rotation. I will stay mostly with improved and hybrid seed, use moderate-to-strong fertilizer on the vegetables and grain, and use less labor-intensive tillage where I can, especially for maize after wheat.
